modules.name: ShortenService
modules.responsibility: Core domain logic: generate short codes for long URLs, enforce uniqueness, resolve codes back to target URLs. Owns the shortening algorithm and collision handling.

modules.name: CodeGenerator
modules.responsibility: Produce short, URL-safe, hard-to-enumerate codes. Encapsulates the encoding scheme (base62 over a counter or random) so it can be swapped without touching domain logic.

modules.name: LinkRepository
modules.responsibility: Persistence boundary for short links and their metadata. Abstracts storage so an in-memory impl serves tests and a SQL/KV impl serves production.
interfaces:
class LinkRepository(Protocol):
    def save(self, link: ShortLink) -> None: ...
    def get_by_code(self, code: str) -> ShortLink | None: ...
    def exists(self, code: str) -> bool: ...
    def delete(self, code: str) -> None: ...

modules.name: StatsCollector
modules.responsibility: Record click events asynchronously and aggregate per-link statistics (total clicks, last accessed, referrer/UA breakdown) without slowing the redirect hot path.

modules.name: RateLimiter
modules.responsibility: Throttle abusive request volume per client identity (IP or API key) on both shorten and redirect endpoints using a token-bucket strategy.
interfaces:
class RateLimiter(Protocol):
    def check(self, identity: str, action: str) -> RateDecision: ...

modules.name: HttpApi
modules.responsibility: HTTP delivery layer: routes POST /shorten, GET /{code} (302 redirect), GET /{code}/stats. Wires middleware (rate limiting) and translates domain results to responses/errors.
interfaces:
class ApiHandler(Protocol):
    def shorten(self, request: Request) -> Response: ...
    def redirect(self, request: Request) -> Response: ...
    def stats(self, request: Request) -> Response: ...
injection_points: all service protocols injected at app composition root

data_model.name: ShortLink

fields.note: API key or hashed IP of creator

relationships: one ShortLink has many ClickEvent (by code)

ux_flows.name: Shorten a URL
steps: Client sends POST /shorten with {long_url, optional custom_alias}
Validate URL format and scheme (http/https only)
ux_flows.success_criteria: Valid URL returns a working short link in a single request, <100ms p95
i18n_considerations: error messages localizable via message keys

ux_flows.name: Follow a short link (redirect)
steps: If active and not expired -> StatsCollector.record_click (async, non-blocking)
ux_flows.success_criteria: Known active code redirects in <30ms p95; stats recorded without blocking redirect

ux_flows.name: View click stats
ux_flows.success_criteria: Owner retrieves accurate aggregate counts; no raw PII exposed

customer_journey: A developer integrating link sharing wants to turn long, ugly URLs into short ones and learn whether anyone clicks them. They POST a long URL and instantly receive a compact short_url. They paste it into a message; recipients click it and are redirected transparently to the destination. Later the developer GETs the stats endpoint to see total clicks, unique visitors, and last-clicked time — enough to judge engagement — without ever handling raw visitor IP addresses. Abusive bulk callers are throttled with clear 429 responses, keeping the service responsive for everyone.

experience_metric.name: shorten_latency_and_steps
experience_metric.target: Shorten a URL in exactly 1 API call with p95 latency ≤100ms; redirect p95 ≤30ms
experience_metric.rationale: Single-call simplicity and sub-30ms redirects keep the link transparent to end users.

architecture_decisions.title: Decouple click-stat recording from the redirect hot path
architecture_decisions.context: The redirect endpoint is latency-critical and the highest-traffic path. Click statistics must be captured, but synchronous DB writes on every redirect would add latency and create a failure dependency: a stats write error must never break a redirect.
architecture_decisions.decision: Make StatsCollector.record_click fire-and-forget. The redirect handler computes the target and returns 302 immediately, dispatching the click event to an async queue/background worker. Stats persistence failures are logged, not surfaced to the redirecting user.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Separation of concerns (SRP) and resilience: redirect correctness is independent of analytics availability. Async decoupling preserves <30ms redirect latency and lets stats storage scale or degrade independently.
consequences: Stats are eventually consistent, not real-time
Need a durable queue or at-least-once buffer to avoid losing clicks on crash
Slightly more operational complexity (worker/queue) but isolated behind the StatsCollector protocol
Redirect path stays simple and fast

architecture_decisions.title: Random base62 codes over sequential counter encoding
architecture_decisions.context: Short codes can be generated from a monotonically increasing counter (compact, predictable) or from random entropy (non-enumerable). Sequential codes leak total link volume and let attackers crawl all links.
architecture_decisions.decision: Generate 7-char random base62 codes with collision-retry against LinkRepository.exists; allow opt-in custom aliases.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Non-enumerability is a privacy/security property; 62^7 (~3.5T) space keeps collisions negligible at expected scale while staying short.
consequences: Need a uniqueness check (extra read) on creation
No information leak about volume or ordering
Custom aliases require separate collision handling

threat_model.description: Open-redirect abuse: attacker shortens links to phishing/malware sites, leveraging the service's trusted domain to bypass user suspicion.
threat_model.mitigation: Validate scheme (http/https only), optional domain denylist/safe-browsing check, show interstitial for flagged links, allow takedown via active=false.

threat_model.description: Flood of shorten or redirect requests exhausts storage/compute and degrades service for legitimate users.
threat_model.mitigation: Token-bucket RateLimiter per IP/API key on all endpoints; return 429; tighter policy on write endpoint than redirect.

threat_model.description: Click stats and stored client IPs reveal who visited which link; enumeration of codes exposes all destinations.
threat_model.mitigation: Random non-enumerable codes; store only salted ip_hash not raw IP; authorize stats reads to creator only; aggregate-only stats responses.

privacy_inventory.purpose: Approximate unique-visitor counts and abuse detection
privacy_inventory.retention: Never stored raw; salted SHA-256 hash retained 90 days then purged
privacy_inventory.encryption: Hashed at ingest (one-way), TLS in transit, encryption at rest for stats store
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Time-based purge job deletes ClickEvent rows >90 days; link deletion cascades click events

privacy_inventory.encryption: Encryption at rest, TLS in transit
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Purged with parent ClickEvent on retention expiry or link deletion

privacy_inventory.purpose: Ownership/authorization for stats and link management
privacy_inventory.encryption: Stored hashed where derived from IP; TLS in transit
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Removed when link is deleted on creator request

i18n_plan.framework: ICU MessageFormat with message-key catalogs per locale
i18n_plan.rtl_strategy: Logical CSS properties and dir=auto for any HTML error/interstitial pages; API responses use neutral keys with localized rendering at the edge
i18n_plan.notes: Accept IDN/punycode target URLs; format dates/numbers in stats per Accept-Language header

open_questions: Do short links expire by default, or persist indefinitely unless a TTL is set?
Is authentication (API keys) in scope for iteration 0, or is creator_identity derived solely from hashed IP?
What is the expected write/read volume — does it justify Redis for rate limiting and a queue for stats, or is in-process sufficient?
Are custom aliases a v0 requirement or deferred?
Is safe-browsing/malware screening of target URLs required, or out of scope?

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: url-shortener exposes three HTTP endpoints — shorten, redirect, stats — behind a token-bucket rate limiter. Domain logic (ShortenService, CodeGenerator) is isolated from delivery (HttpApi) and persistence (LinkRepository, ClickRepository) via Protocols for testability and swappable backends.

sections.title: Module Boundaries
sections.content: Six modules: ShortenService (domain), CodeGenerator (encoding), LinkRepository (link persistence), StatsCollector (async analytics), RateLimiter (throttling), HttpApi (delivery). All cross-module dependencies are injected at a composition root.

sections.title: Data Model
sections.content: ShortLink (code PK, long_url, created_at, creator_identity, expires_at, active). ClickEvent (PII: ip_hash, referrer, user_agent). ClickStats aggregate view. RateBucket for token-bucket state.

sections.title: Key Decisions
sections.content: ADR-001: async fire-and-forget click recording keeps redirect path <30ms and resilient to stats failures. ADR-002: random base62 codes prevent enumeration.

sections.title: Security & Privacy
sections.content: Top threats: open-redirect abuse, DoS, info disclosure. Mitigations: scheme validation, rate limiting, non-enumerable codes, salted IP hashing. PII (IP/UA/referrer) hashed or retained 90 days with time-based purge and cascade erasure on link deletion.
